title: Sophie Calle: Something Missing?
description: Major exhibition by the French conceptual artist Sophie Calle, whose work blends photography, text and personal storytelling around absence, memory and loss. The gallery is open Tuesday to Sunday plus bank holidays, 11am to 5pm, so check the day before travelling. Free weekly drawing tours (Fridays) and family highlight tours (Saturdays) accompany the show.

title: David Hockney: Sunley Window 2026
description: A David Hockney work displayed in Turner Contemporary's Sunley Window, the gallery's changing single-work display space. Its run ends on Sunday 1 November 2026, so the last week of October is the final chance to see it. Free entry during normal gallery hours (Tuesday to Sunday, 11am to 5pm).

title: JMW Turner: Breaking Waves
description: Long-running free display of work by JMW Turner, the painter who loved Margate's skies and gave the gallery its name. It opened in April 2025 and the gallery lists it as continuing into 2027 without a fixed end date, so it can be seen on any normal opening day (Tuesday to Sunday and bank holidays, 11am to 5pm).

title: A Life in Pictures: Martin Gayford on David Hockney
description: Evening talk by art critic and author Martin Gayford, a long-time friend and interviewer of David Hockney, looking back over the painter's life and work. It ties in with the Hockney piece in the gallery's Sunley Window. Tickets are priced on a sliding scale.

title: Family Film Day: Small World Cinema
description: Half-term film day for families. A morning 'Cinemini' session is aimed at children aged two to five, and the afternoon starts with crafts at 1.30pm followed by a screening of 'Alfie, the Little Werewolf' for ages six and up. Booking ahead is advised as family sessions are popular in half term.

title: Drawing Tour: Sophie Calle
booking: Booking advised via the gallery website
description: A free 45-minute guided drawing session through the Sophie Calle exhibition every Friday afternoon. No drawing experience is needed; it is a relaxed way to look closely at the work. Runs weekly from 16 October; the end date is assumed to match the exhibition closing on 24 January 2027.

title: Family Highlight Tour: Sophie Calle
booking: Booking advised via the gallery website
description: Short, free half-hour tour of the Sophie Calle exhibition pitched at families with children, held every Saturday morning from 17 October. The end date is assumed to match the exhibition closing on 24 January 2027. Booking is advised; the tour is a good taster before exploring on your own.

title: BSL Tour: Sophie Calle
description: Tour of the Sophie Calle exhibition delivered in British Sign Language. A second BSL tour is listed for Saturday 9 January 2027 at the same time. The tour is free but the gallery advises booking a place ahead. Turner Contemporary stands on the seafront beside Margate's harbour, a short walk from Margate station; normal gallery hours are Tuesday to Sunday, 11am to 5pm.

title: Audio Described Tour: Sophie Calle
description: Guided tour of the Sophie Calle exhibition with spoken description, designed for blind and partially sighted visitors and their companions. Free, but the gallery advises booking a place. Turner Contemporary stands on the seafront beside Margate's harbour, a short walk from Margate station; normal gallery hours are Tuesday to Sunday, 11am to 5pm.

title: Relaxed Hours: Sophie Calle
description: A quieter hour before normal opening, aimed at visitors who prefer a calmer, less crowded gallery, such as neurodivergent people or anyone sensitive to noise and busy spaces. Free; booking encouraged. Turner Contemporary stands on the seafront beside Margate's harbour, a short walk from Margate station; normal gallery hours are Tuesday to Sunday, 11am to 5pm.

title: Turner: Festive After Hours
description: A late-night Christmas party in the gallery running from 6pm until midnight. It is a ticketed adult evening event priced at £65; see the gallery website for what the ticket includes. Book ahead online; it is a one-night event. Turner Contemporary stands on the seafront beside Margate's harbour, a short walk from Margate station; normal gallery hours are Tuesday to Sunday, 11am to 5pm.

title: Yule! A Feast Through the History of Christmas
description: Seasonal dinner evening at Turner Contemporary on Thursday 3 and Friday 4 December, built around the history of Christmas food and customs. The £80 ticket includes a welcome drink. Places are limited, so book ahead online. Turner Contemporary stands on the seafront beside Margate's harbour, a short walk from Margate station; normal gallery hours are Tuesday to Sunday, 11am to 5pm.

title: Natural Magic: Women, Art, Spirit Worlds
description: Spring 2027 exhibition about esotericism, spiritualism and feminism in the work of more than 30 women artists, from the 19th century to today, in drawing, painting, sculpture, film and installation. Curated by Jennifer Higgie with Melissa Blanchflower and inspired by Higgie's book 'The Other Side'. Names include Georgiana Houghton and Leonora Carrington.

title: Dreamland half-term opening
price: Ride wristbands half price through October (see website)
description: Margate's historic seafront amusement park opens daily over October half term. Rides run 11am to 4pm (3pm on Sunday 1 November) and the indoor Roller Room is open 10.30am to 3.45pm. On Saturday 24 October the front doors close at 2pm for an evening event, so use the Belgrave Road car park entrance. Winter opening after half term was not published.

title: Breakin' Science & Drumatics: Halloween Warm Up
price: From £13.30 early bird plus fee; 18+ with ID
description: Adults-only drum and bass Halloween party in Dreamland's Hall by the Sea, running from late afternoon into the evening. Fancy dress is in the spirit of the night. Strictly 18+ with ID. On this day the park's front doors close at 2pm; enter via Belgrave Road car park or the gates off Hall By The Sea Road.

title: Princess Proms
description: Family concert themed around fairy-tale princesses, the kind of show where children often come dressed up. Two shows, at 12.45pm and 3.30pm. Suitable from age two. Ticket prices were not listed on the venue page; booking fees apply. Dreamland is on Marine Terrace facing Margate Main Sands, a few minutes' walk from Margate station; check the age guidance before booking.

title: Sleeping Beauty (family show)
description: A Christmas-season family version of Sleeping Beauty staged indoors at Dreamland over one weekend. Performances on Friday 4 December at 6pm, and Saturday 5 and Sunday 6 December at 1pm and 5pm. Suitable for ages two and over. Booking is recommended.

title: GirlyPop Live's Short 'n' Sweetmas
description: Christmas-themed pop party show for younger fans. Dreamland lists it as suitable from age four. Check the website for the start time. Ticket prices were not listed; transaction and booking fees apply. Dreamland is on Marine Terrace facing Margate Main Sands, a few minutes' walk from Margate station; check the age guidance before booking.

title: Martin Kemp: Back to the 80s Xmas Special
description: Christmas edition of Martin Kemp's 1980s DJ night, the Spandau Ballet bassist and actor playing decade-defining hits. An adults-only (18+) night out in Dreamland's venue. Booking fees apply. Dreamland is on Marine Terrace facing Margate Main Sands, a few minutes' walk from Margate station; check the age guidance before booking.

title: Halloween Half Term Bash at Margate Caves
description: Margate's 18th-century hand-dug caves host a half-term ghost trail, included in normal admission (last entry 4.30pm). Extras: 'Messy Monday' bat crafts on 26 October (drop in 11am to 4pm, £2 per child) and Halloween face painting on 31 October (2pm to 4pm, £5 per child).

title: Christmas at the Caves: Christmas in Oz
price: £17.95 per child; up to 2 adults free; extra adults £5
description: The caves are dressed as the Land of Oz for a Christmas walk-through with Scarecrow, Tin Man and Lion scenes, ending with a private visit to Father Christmas and a gift for each child. Open 28-29 Nov (10am-3pm), 5-6 and 12-13 Dec, then 18-23 Dec (10am-5pm). Step-free access listed.

title: Oyster Ghouls at the Shell Grotto
description: Half-term drop-in craft session at the Shell Grotto, the mysterious underground passage lined with millions of seashells. Children make spooky creations; the activity is included in the usual admission price. The grotto is in Grotto Hill, a short walk uphill from Margate Old Town. A nice rainy-day pairing with Margate Caves nearby.

title: Halloween at the Old Kent Market Asylum
description: The Old Kent Market, a food and drink hall in a former cinema building by Margate's Old Town, turns into a Halloween 'asylum' from midday on 31 October. Details beyond the theme and start time were not published. It is on Fort Hill, a short walk from Turner Contemporary.

title: Bongo's Bingo: Halloween Special
description: Rowdy adult bingo-meets-rave night in fancy dress at The Drill Shed on the Cliftonville Lido site. Doors at 6pm, first game at 7pm. 18+ with ID. Costumes are part of the fun. Book ahead online; the Drill Shed is on the Cliftonville seafront by Walpole Bay.

title: Tom Thumb Theatre Christmas Night Market
description: Evening Christmas market at the tiny Tom Thumb Theatre on Cliftonville's Eastern Esplanade. Listed dates: 25 November and 2, 9, 10, 16 and 18 December 2026. The listing also says 'every Wednesday', but 10 and 18 December are not Wednesdays, so confirm with the theatre before going.

title: Cliftonville Farmers' Market
description: Award-winning volunteer-run farmers' market with over 50 stalls on the clifftop green at Palm Bay: bread, cheese, raw honey, game, free-range meat and eggs, juices and vegetables, including vegan and gluten-free stalls. Held on the last Sunday of the month. December has an earlier Christmas market instead (20 December 2026, listed separately). Free parking on Palm Bay Avenue.

title: Cliftonville Farmers' Christmas Market
description: December's Cliftonville Farmers' Market is held a week early, on Sunday 20 December, so you can buy local meat, cheese, bread and other produce for Christmas. Times are assumed to be the usual 10am to 1pm. Free parking along Palm Bay Avenue. Contact: cliftonvillefm.co.uk.

title: Margate parkrun
price: Free (register once at parkrun.org.uk and bring your barcode)
description: Free, volunteer-run, timed 5km run or walk every Saturday at 9am on the clifftop at Palm Bay, Cliftonville. All abilities are welcome, including walkers. Register once online and bring your barcode. Volunteers meet at 8.45am. The course is on Cliftonville's clifftop lawns with sea views; dress for the wind in winter.

title: Margate Remembrance Sunday parade and service
description: Expected: the 2026 timetable had not been published by 23 October. In 2025 the parade formed at St Paul's Church, Northdown Road, at 10.30am and marched to the War Memorial in Trinity Gardens for a service from about 10.55am with the two-minute silence at 11am, followed by a salute on The Parade. Organised by the Mayor of Margate and Charter Trustees; expect morning road closures.

title: Christmas in Margate (tree lights switch-on)
description: Expected: date not yet announced. Estimated from 2025, when the Mayor and Charter Trustees ran a free day on Margate High Street and The Piazza on Saturday 29 November (11am to 4pm) with a free grotto, carols at 4.30pm and the Christmas tree lights switched on at 5pm. 2025 was the event's fifth year.

title: Broadstairs Firework Night
description: The town council's free Bonfire Night display over Viking Bay, by the bandstand. Live music from 6pm to 8pm (The SuperMicks, Gianni Scalera and The Jury), and fireworks by Viking Fireworks start at 7pm sharp. Roads nearby close with no parking 5.30pm to 7pm, so walk or come by train. Wrap up warm; hot food and drinks on sale.

title: Broadstairs Remembrance Service
description: Broadstairs & St Peter's Town Council's Service of Remembrance at the war memorial beside Pierremont Park on the High Street. Parts of the service are signed and the hymns led by Inspiration Creative, so it is accessible to hearing-impaired visitors. Groups wishing to lay a wreath must register with the council by noon on 6 November.

title: Broadstairs Christmas Market
description: The town council's Christmas market at Pierremont Hall and Park on the High Street, with stalls from local traders, makers and food vendors, plus live music and food and drink. There is no parking on site. Pierremont Hall is on Broadstairs High Street, a few minutes' walk from Broadstairs station.

title: Halloween Boo Bash
booking: Register with the town council's events team
description: The town council's free Halloween party for children aged three to twelve at Pierremont Hall, in two sessions: noon to 2pm and 3pm to 5pm. Places must be registered in advance. The council also runs a free Hocus Pocus film night for ages 13-17 from 6pm the same evening.

title: Trash to Treasure Halloween craft workshop
description: Free half-term craft session at Pierremont Hall where children turn recycled materials into Halloween decorations. Run by Broadstairs & St Peter's Town Council; no booking, first come first served. Pierremont Hall is on the High Street, about five minutes' walk from Broadstairs station.

title: Pumpkin carving at Westwood Cross
booking: Eventbrite (search 'halloween pumpkin carving at Westwood Cross')
description: Four 45-minute pumpkin-carving sessions at Thanet's main shopping centre, starting at 10am, 11am, noon and 1pm. Under-18s must have a parent or guardian with them, one adult per child. Westwood Cross has large free car parks and is served by many Thanet bus routes.

title: Santa's Grotto at Westwood Cross
description: Santa's grotto at the Westwood Cross shopping centre for the Christmas shopping season. Visit Thanet lists it from 27 November to Christmas Eve 2026 (its title says 2027 by mistake). Check the centre for session times and prices. A handy indoor option if the weather is bad.

title: Cinderella (pantomime)
price: Advance: adult £26, child £24, family £96; door: adult £28, child £26
description: The Sarah Thorne Theatre's 15th annual traditional family pantomime, with matinees from 12 to 31 December. Matinees start at 2.30pm. Step-free access and accessible parking are listed. The theatre is on Fordoun Road, Broadstairs; tickets are cheaper in advance than on the door.

title: The Haunted Bride
description: A one-night Halloween-week ghost story performance at the Sarah Thorne Theatre in Broadstairs. Tickets are £2 cheaper bought in advance from the theatre's website. The Sarah Thorne Theatre is on Fordoun Road, Broadstairs, with step-free access and accessible parking listed.

title: Santa Specials at Crampton Tower
venue: Crampton Tower Museum, The Broadway (by Broadstairs station)
price: £16 per child; up to 2 adults free; extra adults £5
description: Weekend Christmas visits at the small engineering museum in the old Crampton water tower: climb through the elves' workshop to meet Father Christmas. Each child (up to 11) gets a gift and, weather permitting, a ride on the 5-inch-gauge miniature railway. Saturdays and Sundays 5-6, 12-13 and 19-20 December.

title: The Signalman at Dickens House Museum
description: A short abridged performance of Charles Dickens's ghost story 'The Signalman' in the clifftop house that inspired Betsey Trotwood's home in David Copperfield. Showings at 1.30pm, 2.30pm and 3.30pm; the museum is open 1pm to 4pm. Normal museum admission covers the performance.

title: Halloween Treat: Nadja (15)
description: Halloween-night 'treat' screening of the film 'Nadja' (certificate 15) at the Palace, a 111-seat independent cinema in a listed building on Harbour Street, a minute from Viking Bay. Book online; seating is limited in this small cinema, which has about 111 seats across stalls and balcony.

title: Sunday Silent: South (1919)
description: Part of the Palace Cinema's Sunday Silent series: Frank Hurley's documentary of Shackleton's Antarctic expedition, 'South' (1919). The previous title in the series was 'The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari' on 25 October. Check the cinema's website for the screening time and any live accompaniment.

title: Palace Cinema, Broadstairs (daily screenings)
description: Single-screen independent cinema in a Grade II listed building on Harbour Street, run by owners with a background in independent film. It shows new independent and world cinema plus special events such as silent films with live piano and dementia-friendly screenings. Good for a rainy afternoon; check the website for showtimes.

title: Broadstairs New Year's Day Dip
description: Expected: no 2027 announcement yet. A Broadstairs tradition since 2002: dippers gather at a pub near the harbour and plunge into Viking Bay at midday, many in fancy dress, raising money for the Children's Liver Disease Foundation. In recent years swimmers met at The George Inn by 11am-11.30am, though one report says it moved to the Dolphin Inn. Rough seas have led to changes before.

title: Frankenstein 1930
venue: The Centre (Birchington Village Centre), Alpha Road
description: Stage version of the Frankenstein story by the Leaky Brain company, set in 1930, at Birchington's village centre hall on Alpha Road. Evening performances to Saturday 24 October. The Centre is next to Birchington Library, a few minutes' walk from Birchington-on-Sea station.

title: Halloween Family Disco
venue: The Centre (Birchington Village Centre), Alpha Road
description: Halloween disco for families at The Centre in Birchington. Doors open at 6pm. Children's tickets should be bought in advance; adults go free. The Centre is on Alpha Road in the village centre, next to Birchington Library, with a pay-and-display car park nearby.

title: Trick or Treat Trail at Quex
venue: Quex Adventure Farm Park, Park Lane
description: Half-term Halloween trail at Quex Adventure Farm Park. The ticket covers the trail, a treat, one pumpkin per child and a ride on the Slime Blaster Express. Combine with the pumpkin patch (to 31 October). Book online; free car parking at Quex.

title: Pumpkin Patch at Quex
venue: Quex Adventure Farm Park, Park Lane
description: Pick-your-own pumpkin patch at Quex Adventure Farm Park on the Quex estate, just south of Birchington village. Runs until Halloween. Prices vary by ticket type. Quex Adventure Farm Park is on Park Lane, Birchington, with free parking and walking routes from the village.

title: Halloween Fest! at Quex (14+)
venue: Quex Adventure Farm Park, Park Lane
description: After-dark scare event for ages 14 and over with three new scare mazes and live entertainment. Runs on three nights only: Saturday 24, Friday 30 and Saturday 31 October. Not suitable for younger children. Book online; free parking on site.

title: Quex Park Bonfire & Fireworks
description: Large bonfire and fireworks display in the grounds of Quex Park, just off the A28 south of Birchington. The organisers' site says 'Join us on the 1st of November'; gate and display times and prices were not shown on 23 October, so check before going. Parking marshals on site.

title: A Cosy Quex House Christmas
description: Christmas season at Quex House, the Powell-Cotton family's Regency country house at the heart of the Quex estate, next to the Powell-Cotton Museum. Visit Thanet lists it from 21 November to 13 December 2026; opening days, times and prices were not given, so check with Quex Park.

title: The Elf Express
venue: Quex Adventure Farm Park, Park Lane
description: Christmas experience at Quex Adventure Farm Park: a tractor ride through elf woods, real reindeer, a personal visit with Santa, Candy Cane Lane and Santa's toy shop, with festive food and lights. Open 5-6, 12-13 and 16-24 December only. Free parking.

title: Skate Into Quex (ice rink)
venue: Quex Adventure Farm Park, Park Lane
description: Real ice rink at Quex Adventure Farm Park, open rain or shine, for toddlers to adults and beginners to experienced skaters. Around it is a Christmas village of giant tipis with an elves' toy shop, crafts, a lounge and a hot chocolate bar. Open daily noon to 8pm, closed Christmas Day and Boxing Day.

title: Quex Christmas tree lighting
venue: Quex Adventure Farm Park, Park Lane
description: Expected: the 2026 date is not announced. Estimated from 2025, when Quex Adventure Farm Park held a free ticketed evening on Sunday 30 November (4.30pm to 7pm) with ice skating from 5pm, carol singing and the tree lit at 6pm. The rink opens on 30 November 2026, so the date may change.

title: Birchington at Christmas (village day and lights switch-on)
price: Free; children's activities need a 'Birchington Express' ticket (£3.50 in 2025)
description: Expected: the organisers say it returns in 2026 but have not published the date. In 2025 it was on Saturday 29 November, 10am to 6pm across The Square, Dog Acre and The Centre, with Santa visits and the lights switched on at 5.30pm. In 2024 a children's lantern parade walked to Dog Acre for a 6pm switch-on. Run by Birchington Traders Together and Birchington Parish Council.

title: Birchington Remembrance Sunday parade and service
description: Expected: the 2026 details were not published by 23 October. In 2025 the parade ran from Station Road to The Square, 10.30am to noon. Older listings describe a Royal British Legion parade, wreath-laying at 11am at the war memorial outside All Saints Church (a Grade II listed WWI cross bearing 69 names), then a service in the church.

title: Birchington Farmers' Market
description: Monthly farmers' market on Dog Acre green in the village centre, held on the third Sunday of each month. It was saved from closure in 2026 by Sally and Colin Pitcher of Pitchers' Preserves. Pay-and-display parking is behind the green. No winter break was mentioned; check before travelling in deep winter.

title: Minnis Bay New Year's Day Dip
venue: Minnis Bay (slope by The Minnis restaurant)
description: Expected: informal community dip, no 2027 notice found. The last published listing (for 1 January 2024) had dippers meeting at 2pm at the slope by The Minnis restaurant, with the Birchington 'Bluetits' swimming group meeting at 2.30pm. Times usually depend on the tide, so check local groups closer to the day and never swim in rough conditions.

title: Westgate Remembrance Sunday parade and service
description: The town council has confirmed a parade from St Saviour's Church to the War Memorial on Sea Road, followed by a Service of Remembrance there at noon. Roads close during the parade. In 2025 church services began at 10.30am and the parade moved off at 11.45am, ending with tea at Christ Church URC.

title: Westgate Late Night Christmas Shopping
description: Westgate's independent shops stay open until 8pm, with discounts and mince pies. A relaxed way to start Christmas shopping in a small seaside town centre. Organised with Westgate-on-Sea Town Council. Westgate station is in the heart of the shopping streets.

title: Westgate Christmas Lights Switch-On Fair
description: Expected: 2026 date not yet published. Estimated from recent years, when the fair filled Station Road on a Sunday (30 November 2025, 1 December 2024) from 11am to 5pm, with a street market, two music stages, funfair rides, a Santa parade and grotto, and the lights switched on at about 4.30pm.

title: Carlton Cinema, Westgate (daily screenings)
description: Three-screen cinema in a Grade II listed 1910 building, built as a town hall and showing films since 1912, now run by Picturedrome. It shows new releases plus baby-friendly, sensory and subtitled screenings, 'Film and Fizz' nights and opera/ballet broadcasts. Christmas 2026 titles include The Polar Express pyjama party and Elf.

title: Westgate Christmas Day Dip
description: Expected: no 2026 notice yet. In 2024 the Westgate Wetsuits swimming group held an early Christmas morning dip at West Bay at around 8am. Check the group's social media first, and only swim if conditions are safe. West Bay is the sandy beach below Sea Road.

title: Westgate New Year's Day Dip
description: Expected: not yet announced. For 1 January 2025 the Westgate Wetsuits group met at West Bay around midday, and an unofficial dip took place at St Mildred's Bay at high tide (12.30pm in an earlier year). Times often follow the tide, so check locally.

title: Ramsgate Remembrance Sunday parade and service
description: The parade moves off from outside Chatham & Clarendon Grammar School at 10.35am and marches through Chatham Street, High Street, King Street, Broad Street and Church Hill to St George's Church, Ramsgate's landmark Georgian church with its tall lantern tower, for wreath-laying and a Service of Remembrance.

title: Ramsgate Armistice Day services
description: Armistice Day observances on Wednesday 11 November: wreath-laying at the Destiny War Memorial in Albion Gardens at 9am, then a short service and two-minute silence in the town centre at 11am. At the same time the Royal British Legion lays wreaths at Ramsgate Cemetery.

title: Ramsgate Winter Festival
description: Two-month festival of light, art, music and community events around Ramsgate town and its Royal Harbour, with the 2026 theme 'Spark, Gather, Grow'. Highlights: the lights switch-on (29 Nov), a Weekend of Wonder (11-13 Dec), the Light Up Ramsgate window trail, a New Year's Eve lantern parade and the New Year's Day dip. Full programme due in November.

title: Ramsgate Christmas Lights Switch-On
description: Opening day of the Ramsgate Winter Festival: a Handmade & Vintage Christmas Market, a samba parade with Samba Ya Wantsum, and the town lights switched on at about 4.30pm, followed by a procession to St George's Church for 'Let There Be Light'. The Dame Janet Makers Market runs the same day.

title: Ramsgate Weekend of Wonder
description: Festive weekend in the town centre: late-night shopping on Friday 11 December, projected light creatures, the Christmas Tree Festival in St George's Church, special events at Ramsgate Tunnels and the launch of the Light Up Ramsgate window trail. Boat owners also light up their vessels in the Royal Harbour during December.

title: Light Up Ramsgate
description: Winter trail of light installations, projections and illuminated artworks in shop windows and venues across Ramsgate town centre, by local and international artists. Run by HOLD Creative Spaces as part of the Ramsgate Winter Festival. Best seen after dark. Free to walk round.

title: Christmas Baroque concert
description: Baroque Christmas music concert in St George's Church, part of the Ramsgate Winter Festival programme. Time and ticket details are due when the full programme is released in November. St George's Church is at the top of Church Hill in the town centre.

title: Ramsgate New Year's Eve Lantern Parade
description: Free family lantern parade from St George's Church, past the harbour, to a celebration outside Ramsgate Tunnels on Marina Esplanade. The 2026 start time is not yet published; in 2025 walkers met at 4.15pm at St George's Church. Bring a lantern.

title: Ramsgate New Year's Day Dip
venue: Ramsgate Main Sands (meet at the Queen's Head)
description: Charity sea dip on Ramsgate Main Sands, listed in the Winter Festival programme for 1 January. Time not yet confirmed. In previous years dippers met at the Queen's Head on Harbour Parade from 11am and ran into the sea at noon, with medals for all and fancy-dress prizes. The dip has been postponed in bad weather before.

title: Jack and the Beanstalk (family pantomime)
description: Ramsgate's Christmas family pantomime at the Granville Theatre, a seafront theatre-cinema on Victoria Parade. Runs 12-24 December; individual performance times are on the booking page. A relaxed performance is on Saturday 19 December at 10am. Prices are shown when booking.

title: Jack and the Beanstalk: Relaxed Performance
description: A relaxed performance of the Granville's family pantomime, with gentler sound and lighting and a more forgiving atmosphere for anyone who finds a normal theatre visit difficult. Booking is through the theatre's website. The Granville is on Victoria Parade on Ramsgate's East Cliff; the box office is on 01843 594510 and prices are shown when you book.

title: Halloween – In Concert
description: Live concert of spooky music for Halloween week at the Granville Theatre, with a prize for the best costume. Book online; booking fees apply. The Granville is on Victoria Parade on Ramsgate's East Cliff; the box office is on 01843 594510 and prices are shown when you book.

title: The Overtones: Jivin' Home For Christmas
description: The vocal harmony group The Overtones bring their Christmas tour show to the Granville Theatre on Ramsgate's seafront. Performance runs about 7.30pm to 9.45pm. The Granville is on Victoria Parade on Ramsgate's East Cliff; the box office is on 01843 594510 and prices are shown when you book.

title: Snow White and the Seven Inches (adult panto)
description: Touring adults-only pantomime full of innuendo, on Friday 22 and Saturday 23 January 2027 at 8pm. Strictly over-18s. Not for children. The Granville is on Victoria Parade on Ramsgate's East Cliff; the box office is on 01843 594510 and prices are shown when you book.

title: Family Halloween Tour at Ramsgate Tunnels
description: Halloween family tour of Ramsgate Tunnels, the miles of wartime air-raid shelters and old railway tunnel in the chalk cliffs. For ages five and up. The tunnels entrance is on Marina Esplanade at the foot of the East Cliff; booking online is advised as tours have limited places.

title: The Signalman, performed by Gerald Dickens
description: Gerald Dickens, great-great-grandson of Charles Dickens, performs his ancestor's railway ghost story in the old railway tunnel, followed by a Q&A. Shows at 5pm and 7pm; arrive 30 minutes early. Booking online is advised. The tunnels entrance is on Marina Esplanade below the East Cliff.

title: Halloween at Ellington Park
description: Community Halloween evening in Ramsgate's Ellington Park with a free storytelling walk at 6pm and a fancy-dress competition (register by 6pm). Some activities depend on the weather. Ellington Park is a Victorian park a short walk from Ramsgate station. Free to visit; bring a torch.

title: Newington Community Halloween Fayre
description: Small community Halloween fair in Ramsgate with local traders, face painting, glitter tattoos and activities for children. Free entry. The community centre is on Princess Margaret Avenue in the Newington area of Ramsgate, a short bus ride from the town centre. A low-key, budget-friendly option for families during half term.

title: Santa's Grotto Experience at Ramsgate Garden Centre
description: Christmas grotto visits with Father Christmas at Ramsgate Garden Centre, from 28 November to Christmas Eve 2026. Check with the garden centre for session times, prices and booking. Booking is likely to be needed in December; the garden centre is on the Broadstairs side of Ramsgate.

title: Ramsgate Friday Market
description: Weekly street market in Ramsgate town centre every Friday, 9am to 3pm. Combine it with a walk down to the Royal Harbour. Free to browse; stall numbers vary with the weather and the season, so it is quieter in deep winter.

title: Manston Airfield Sunday Market
description: Large Sunday market and car boot run by Stevens Markets on the former Manston airfield, with over 100 stalls, food vans and toilets. Dogs on leads welcome. Arrive early for the best finds; the ground can get muddy after heavy rain, which makes it hard going for wheelchairs and scooters.

title: MOS Productions Christmas pantomime
description: Expected: 2026 title and dates not yet found. Margate Operatic Society (MOS Productions) has staged its annual panto at St Lawrence College, Ramsgate, since the Winter Gardens closed in 2022; in 2025 it was Robin Hood on 17-20 December. Estimated dates follow that pattern.

title: The All-New Adventures of Peter Pan (pantomime)
description: Canterbury's main family pantomime at the Marlowe Theatre, the city's large modern theatre on the riverside by The Friars. The cast appears at the city's lights switch-on on 13 November. Accessible performances are planned, including one on Sunday 3 January 2027 at 1pm.

title: The Reluctant Dragon
description: A brand-new family musical at the Marlowe about friendship and unlikely heroes, It runs alongside the pantomime over the Christmas holidays; see the Marlowe website for times and age guidance. The Marlowe is on The Friars in central Canterbury, close to the Christmas market sites.

title: Canterbury Christmas Market
venue: Whitefriars, St George's Street and Cathedral precincts
description: One of Kent's biggest Christmas markets, with wooden huts spread across St George's Street, Whitefriars and the Cathedral precincts, plus a carousel, live music and Santa visits. Official opening hours were not published by 23 October; third-party guides suggest roughly 10am-6pm on weekdays, so check before travelling.

title: Canterbury Christmas Lights Switch-On
venue: Canterbury city centre (Westgate Square to Burgate)
description: City-wide evening of staggered switch-ons organised by Canterbury BID: a Victorian Christmas in Burgate (lights 6pm, with 'A Christmas Carol'), an artisan market at Westgate Hall (6.30pm), and Westgate Square with Marlowe panto stars (7pm), when the High Street and all market sites light up. Crafts at the Beaney and live music around town.

title: Handel's Messiah by Candlelight
description: Candlelit performance of Handel's Messiah in the nave of Canterbury Cathedral, mother church of the Anglican Communion and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Book ahead online. The cathedral's seasonal services are free with a retiring collection; arrive early for popular services, and note there is no on-site parking at Christmas.

title: Advent Carol Service
description: Candlelit Advent service of readings and music on Advent Sunday, beginning the cathedral's Christmas season. Free, in person and livestreamed. The cathedral's seasonal services are free with a retiring collection; arrive early for popular services, and note there is no on-site parking at Christmas.

title: Cathedral drop-in family Christmas crafts
description: Drop-in Christmas craft sessions for families on the four Saturdays 28 November, 5, 12 and 19 December. Included with a valid cathedral admission ticket. On 5 and 12 December the cathedral archives and library also hold Christmas open days. Combine with the Christmas market stalls in the precincts.

title: St Nicholas Family Service
description: Short family service in the nave around St Nicholas's Day, aimed at children but open to all. Free, in person and livestreamed. The cathedral's seasonal services are free with a retiring collection; arrive early for popular services, and note there is no on-site parking at Christmas.

title: Festival of Carols
description: Family-friendly carol service in the nave with a living nativity and music from the Canterbury Youth Choir. Free, in person and livestreamed. The cathedral's seasonal services are free with a retiring collection; arrive early for popular services, and note there is no on-site parking at Christmas.

title: Cathedral Carol Services by candlelight
booking: No tickets; first come, first seated
description: The cathedral's main candlelit carol services on 23 and 24 December. Unticketed and very popular: doors open at 4.30pm and seats go first come, first served, so arrive early. No on-site parking. Midnight Mass and a morning Family Crib Service follow on Christmas Eve.

title: Midnight Mass
description: Midnight Mass on Christmas Eve, in person and livestreamed. Earlier the same day, a Family Crib Service runs from 10am to 10.45am. The cathedral's seasonal services are free with a retiring collection; arrive early for popular services, and note there is no on-site parking at Christmas.

title: Christmas Day Eucharist and Evensong with Carols
description: Christmas Day Eucharist at 11am, led by the Archbishop of Canterbury, Sarah Mullally, the first woman in the role. Evensong with Carols follows at 3pm. Both are free and open to all, and are livestreamed. No on-site parking at Christmas.

title: Epiphany Carol Service
description: Candlelit carol service for Epiphany, closing the cathedral's Christmas season. Free, in person and livestreamed. The Epiphany Sung Eucharist is on Wednesday 6 January at 5.30pm. The cathedral's seasonal services are free with a retiring collection; arrive early for popular services, and note there is no on-site parking at Christmas.

title: Goldilocks and the Three Bears (pantomime)
venue: The Malthouse theatre, St Edmund's School
description: Smaller-scale family pantomime at The Malthouse, a theatre on the St Edmund's School site in Canterbury. A more intimate alternative to the Marlowe's show. Check the venue for times and tickets. Booking ahead is wise in the school holidays, when family shows sell well.

title: Sylvanian Families Christmas Window Trail
venue: The Beaney House of Art & Knowledge
description: Free children's trail around Canterbury's shops: pick up a trail card at The Beaney House of Art & Knowledge on the High Street, collect stamps from eight participating shops' Sylvanian Families window displays, then claim a prize at Fenwick. Good for keeping children busy during a Christmas market visit.

title: There's a Monster in Your Christmas Show
description: Interactive children's Christmas show at the Gulbenkian arts centre on the University of Kent campus overlooking Canterbury. Check the venue for performance times. The Gulbenkian also has a cinema, a bar and a pay-and-display car park; check the venue for times and prices.

title: The Goods Shed farmers' market and food hall
venue: The Goods Shed, Station Road West
description: Permanent farmers' market and food hall in a Victorian railway goods shed beside Canterbury West station, running since 2002. Stalls include a greengrocer, butcher, fishmonger, cheesemaker, bakery and wine, with a restaurant overlooking the market. Open Tuesday to Sunday, closed Mondays; check opening times on its website.

title: Herne Bay Christmas Lights Switch-On
venue: Herne Bay town centre and seafront
description: Expected: 2026 date not found. Estimated from 2025, when the volunteer-run event was held on Sunday 16 November, 1pm to 6pm, drawing over 3,000 people. The organisers were crowdfunding the £20,000+ cost in 2026, so check that it is going ahead.

title: Herne Bay Community and Farmers' Market
description: Expected schedule: a food directory lists a community and farmers' market in Herne Bay on the first and third Saturday of each month, but the organiser's current timetable was not found. Check locally before making a special trip. The market area is in the town centre near the seafront.
